page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.metal is a bare-metal instance designed for graphics-intensive and compute-heavy workloads. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

The instance integrates eight NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs, delivering a combined 128 GB of VRAM. For local storage, it includes 1800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, optimizing data transfer rates for distributed tasks and EBS volumes.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory bandwidth, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. It also demonstrates strong performance in Passmark CPU extended instructions, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. However, single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression tasks fall into the average category, indicating that workloads relying heavily on single-thread speed may experience a relative bottleneck compared to parallelized tasks.

Given its high density of eight GPUs, dedicated bare-metal CPU resources, and fast local NVMe storage, the instance offers high resource density for parallel processing. It is suited for workloads such as multi-GPU machine learning inference, video transcoding, graphics rendering, large-scale database operations, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services g4dn.metal is a bare-metal, GPU-accelerated server designed for graphics-intensive and highly parallelized compute workloads. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores at 2.5 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The hardware configuration includes eight NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs with a total of 128 GB VRAM, alongside 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and excellent database throughput, though single-core execution speeds remain average. This instance is optimized for multi-GPU machine learning inference, video rendering, and high-throughput database operations.
